curriculum.lesson_evidence: A dance showcase is a performance of your best work at the end of a unit. Prepare by choosing a piece, rehearsing it several times and planning the start and the end shapes. Name the dance elements you used so the audience knows what to watch for. After the showcase, reflect on what went well, which elements were most effective and what you will do next time. Keep your feedback specific and kind. If a performance is not possible, you may describe or draw the dance and give a talk.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write a two-sentence introduction for a dance you could perform, naming the title and two elements.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'My dance is called Waves. It uses slow, curved movements at a low level and quick, high jumps for the big wave.' The introduction names the title and two elements, which helps the audience watch closely.

WATCH FOR
Believing that a showcase means including every movement you know. It is better to show a clear, well-rehearsed piece that uses a few elements with confidence.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Rehearse your best dance from this unit and perform it for family. Introduce it with the title and two elements. Ask for two stars and a wish, and write a reflection with one thing to keep and one thing to practise next.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: Ravi's showcase has a short introduction: 'My dance is called Wind. I use quick, high movements and slow, low ones.' He performs, holds his final shape and bows. His reflection reads: 'Star: I stayed in time with the music. Star: my changes of level were clear. Wish: next time I will stretch my arms more.'

TRY FIRST
Write a two-sentence introduction for a dance you could perform, naming the title and two elements.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'My dance is called Waves. It uses slow, curved movements at a low level and quick, high jumps for the big wave.' The introduction names the title and two elements, which helps the audience watch closely.
teach_steps.explain:
A dance showcase is a performance of your best work at the end of a unit. Prepare by choosing a piece, rehearsing it several times and planning the start and the end shapes. Name the dance elements you used so the audience knows what to watch for. After the showcase, reflect on what went well, which elements were most effective and what you will do next time. Keep your feedback specific and kind. If a performance is not possible, you may describe or draw the dance and give a talk.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the elements, techniques or performance choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For movement or instruments, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby and stop if anything feels unsafe. You may always describe a choice instead of performing it. One deliberate artistic choice with a named effect is more useful than a longer praise sentence.

teaching.fix: Name the element or technique and its effect, not just decoration.
teaching.guided_attempt: Make or describe one fresh example that uses the same skill and write a short reason for your main choice.
teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new artwork or performance.
teaching.model: A dance showcase is a performance of your best work at the end of a unit. Prepare by choosing a piece, rehearsing it several times and planning the start and the end shapes. Name the dance elements you used so the audience knows what to watch for. After the showcase, reflect on what went well, which elements were most effective and what you will do next time. Keep your feedback specific and kind. If a performance is not possible, you may describe or draw the dance and give a talk. Now choose a different subject or piece to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same arts idea in a new artwork, song, drama or dance, not a copy of the example. Review clarity, safety and respectful practice.
